title: Office — your changes, and how long versions are kept

steps.path: A conversation → Session files → Garden plan.docx → Edit
steps.headline: Open in Office is now the briefcase in the panel's header, and a document's text fills the panel's width.

steps.headline: How long should Office keep earlier versions of a file?
steps.today: Office saves every change straight to the file and keeps a copy when you open it and every few minutes while you work.
steps.problem: Without limits those copies pile up forever and fill your disk, especially for big spreadsheets edited daily.
steps.proposal: Three keeping rules. The oldest copies go first whenever a limit is reached.

options.label: A day, then daily
options.summary: Every copy from the last 24 hours, then one per day for 30 days; at most 50 per file and 1 GB for all of Office.
pros: Fine-grained undo for today's work, and a month of daily restore points.
Disk use has a hard ceiling.
cons: A version from 31 days ago is gone.

options.label: One week
options.summary: Every copy for 7 days, then deleted; 1 GB ceiling.
cons: Nothing older than a week can be restored.

options.label: Until you delete
options.summary: Keep everything; a Clear button in Settings empties it.
pros: Nothing is ever lost by accident.
cons: Disk use grows without limit until you notice.

steps.path: Inside the editor: File → Version History
steps.headline: The editor's own Version History menu is hidden; Office's Versions button is the one place to see and restore versions.
steps.changed: OnlyOffice's history panel only works with OnlyOffice's own server storing versions. YouCoded runs no such server, so inside the app that panel would be empty or broken.
steps.notice: One history, in YouCoded's style, the same for documents, spreadsheets and slides.
